_comment: Copy this file to <project>/.claude/ballast.rules.json (project rules) or ~/.claude/ballast.rules.json (user rules). Project rules override user rules on duplicate ids. Keywords are literal substring matches — pair them in every language you chat in, as these examples pair English with Korean and Chinese. Keep bodies short and imperative — every injected character competes with the actual work. To inject a rule into every request regardless of keywords, set "when": {"always": true} — use it for at most one or two rules; an always-on rule you stop reading is worse than no rule, and the session-start status line counts how many you have.

rules.title: Label every claim
rules.body: Research results and model knowledge are drafts. Attach a label to every claim before using it: confirmed / observed / assumed / hearsay / unknown. Unlabeled claims must not be presented as fact. See the verify-gate skill for what each label requires.

rules.title: Estimate before spending
rules.body: Anything that spends money or credits: present an estimate and get explicit approval BEFORE executing. No exceptions for small amounts — the habit is the point.

rules.title: Never swap what the user fixed
rules.body: Models, tools, versions, and settings the user explicitly fixed are not yours to change. Propose alternatives with reasons; the user decides. This applies even when you are sure the alternative is better.

rules.title: Record decisions in-session
rules.body: When the user confirms a decision, write it to the decision ledger in the same session (see the decision-ledger skill). Unresolved items go to the open-questions file — registered, not remembered. Zero loss.

rules.title: Blocked: irreversible bulk destruction
rules.body: This request matched a configured danger pattern and was stopped before the agent saw it. This stops the prompt, not the tool: a later turn can still run the same command without these words, so treat blocks as a guardrail, not a sandbox (README, Know the limits). If you really mean it, re-issue the request explicitly, or edit .claude/ballast.rules.json.

rules.title: Say it for the reader
rules.body: Write for the reader, in the reader's language. Cut filler, hedging, and pleasantries; keep grammar markers (particles, postpositions) — they are grammar, not filler. Never drop not/never/no/only, numbers, or units. A technical term gets a one-line plain gloss at first use with the original in parentheses; plain beats pure (쉬운 말 > 순우리말). Security warnings and irreversible actions stay in full sentences. (Rules distilled from the caveman skill's lite mode, MIT, and the KIISE 쉬운 전문용어 principles, easyword.kr/tips.)

rules.title: Compression tools stay out of memory/
rules.body: Do not let a compression tool rewrite ballast memory files. DECISIONS.md is append-only; knowledge entries carry sources and labels; checkpoints carry orders. Compression drops the load-bearing words first — negations, numbers, sources, labels — and the loss is silent. If a file must shrink: keep the original beside it, shorten by hand, and compare part by part before accepting. This is a ballast rule, not a judgment on the tool.
